tier_reason: OCRmyPDF PR #61 (jbarlow83, 2014-01-20) states 371 s vs 216 s for deskew+OCR on 'a mixed bag of files' and that Leptonica's deskew is '30-40x faster' than ImageMagick convert -deskew standalone; no hardware, versions, commands, file set or benchmark code, so numbers without methodology (C).

corrections.caveats: Third-party contributor's pull-request comment and commit message (jbarlow83, OCRmyPDF PR #61, opened 2014-01-20 against fritz-hh's v2.x branch, closed unmerged 2015-07-28). No hardware, no Leptonica/ImageMagick/Tesseract versions, no commands, no file set beyond 'a mixed bag of files', no repeat counts; the PR only says the change was tested (functionally) on OS X 10.9 and Ubuntu 13.10. The commit message attributes the gap to the algorithm: ImageMagick finds the skew angle with a Hough transform, Leptonica with Postl's variance of differential line sums, so the gain is algorithmic rather than implementation speed; the PR also notes ImageMagick sometimes adds a halftone pattern after rotation. ImageMagick ran as the convert binary from OCRmyPDF v2's script while Leptonica was called through a ctypes wrapper, so process-launch overhead is probably part of the ImageMagick side (not stated). The 30-40x figure has no per-file times; the 371 s and 216 s figures include OCR time, so the end-to-end gain is about 40%. Leptonica's own docs claim DWA morphology is 3-4x faster than its own rasterop morphology (an internal comparison, not recorded as a baseline). No comparison against OpenCV or other image libraries was found. Category set to color-and-resampling because the measured operation is skew detection plus rotation, though Leptonica is a general image-analysis library (guessed category was image-codecs).

notes: PR #61 page confirms the 371 s / 216 s (about 40% less total deskew+OCR time) and '30-40x faster' standalone deskew claims verbatim; metadata checked: 2.1k stars, 433 forks, BSD-2-Clause (leptonica-license.txt), last commit 2026-10-02, not archived. Shortcomings: single 2014 anecdote from a third party with no methodology, algorithmic rather than implementation win, probable subprocess overhead on the ImageMagick side, PR never merged.

tier_reason: Independent measurement by the rival rustybuzz port (results committed by its maintainer LaurenzV, July 2024) with public harness benches/src/lib.rs and CPU stated (Apple M1 Pro), but the rustc nightly version and the C++ compiler used for the bundled HarfBuzz are not stated, so not A; B as an independent third-party measurement.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo +nightly bench (#![feature(test)]) with HARFBUZZ_SYS_NO_PKG_CONFIG="", which makes harfbuzz_rs's build.rs skip pkg-config and compile its bundled harfbuzz/src/harfbuzz.cc with the cc crate (-std=c++11, optimization level from cargo's bench profile); rustc nightly version and C++ compiler (presumably Apple clang) not stated. HarfBuzz comes from harfbuzz_rs git rev 43f0fb5 ('update bindings to 9.0', so about HarfBuzz 9.0.0; harfbuzz submodule at commit b8087db). Harness: harfbuzz/rustybuzz benches/src/lib.rs.
corrections.caveats: The only numbers against an outside baseline come from the rival Rust port's own benches (rustybuzz, now under the harfbuzz GitHub org, archived 2026-07-26), not from the HarfBuzz project. The results were committed by rustybuzz maintainer LaurenzV on 2024-07-01..03, against HarfBuzz about 9.0.0 (harfbuzz_rs rev 43f0fb5) and a rustybuzz that predates its later sync to HarfBuzz v10.1.0; both sides are older than current HarfBuzz 14.x, so today's gap may differ. rustybuzz admits it is not a faithful port and that HarfBuzz's 'accelerators and caches' were deliberately left out of it, which explains much of the gap. HarfBuzz is faster on 65 of 70 rows; rustybuzz wins five short-text rows (arabic word_1/2/3 at 0.82x/0.87x/0.82x rb/hb time ratio, english aat_word_1 at 0.42x, hindi aat_word at 0.62x, all derived from page data). Each iteration builds the face and buffer (and for HarfBuzz also an hb_font via harfbuzz_rs::Font::new), so setup cost is included for both sides and HarfBuzz probably rebuilds its lazily loaded table accelerators every call, which likely explains its losses on single-word rows. Successor HarfRust's README says it is 'less than 25% slower than HarfBuzz on most common fonts' but backs it only with a Google spreadsheet that was not reachable (docs.google.com blocked). HarfBuzz's own NEWS and perf/README.md contain only before/after self-comparisons (for example 10.3.0: AAT shaping of LucidaGrande 14.6 ms to 5.9 ms) and no comparison with CoreText, DirectWrite, Uniscribe, ICU or FreeType; no hb-subset versus fonttools figure was found. The listed 'built-in text shaping' baseline therefore has no numbers here. Licence is HarfBuzz's 'Old MIT' (SPDX MIT-Modern-Variant, OSI-approved); some subdirectories carry their own COPYING files.

notes: All quoted rows and the 70-row statistics (geomean 1.76x, median 1.89x, range 0.42x to 4.38x rb/hb, 65 of 70 rows faster) recomputed exactly from benches/README.md; rustybuzz README '1.5-2x slower than harfbuzz' confirmed. Corrections: licence is MIT-Modern-Variant (HarfBuzz 'Old MIT', OSI-approved per SPDX data) rather than MIT; bundled HarfBuzz pinned to about 9.0.0; results date from July 2024. Shortcomings: baseline is a deliberately unoptimized Rust port, not a system shaper; HarfBuzz itself publishes no comparison against CoreText/DirectWrite/ICU; numbers are two years old.

tier_reason: Public harness highway/benchmark/hw_resolution_benchmark.cpp times the original facedetect_cnn and facedetect_hw_cnn in one executable; README states MSVC 19.40.33821.0 Release, the CPU (i7-14700KF) and the command, and COMPILE.md plus highway/CMakeLists.txt give the CMake options and /arch:AVX2 plus _ENABLE_AVX2 flags, so A (first-party, but reproducible).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 19.40.33821.0 (Visual Studio 17 2022), CMake Release config. Highway build per COMPILE.md 'AVX2 x86 hybrid': -DFDT_HW_X86_ARCH=AVX2 -DFDT_HW_ENABLE_HYBRID_CEILING=ON -DFDT_HW_ENABLE_INTRINSICS_COMPARE=ON, Highway 1.3.0; highway/CMakeLists.txt then compiles the Highway kernels with /arch:AVX2 /W4 /permissive- and compiles the original src/facedetectcnn.cpp into the same fdt_hw_resolution_benchmark executable with _ENABLE_AVX2 and /arch:AVX2 (no OpenMP in this build). Rust 1.95.0 release profile with runtime AVX2 dispatch. Benchmark: highway/benchmark/hw_resolution_benchmark.cpp, command fdt_hw_resolution_benchmark.exe images\cnnresult.png 128 28.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the project's own original implementation, not an external incumbent: no comparison against OpenCV FaceDetectorYN, dlib, MTCNN, RetinaFace or any other detector appears in the README, opencv_dnn/ (deployment demos only), COMPILE.md or the Rust report. All numbers are first-party and the Highway section is recent (added 2026-05-04 by maintainer Wwupup in 'feature: add highway optimize version for 6.4x speed up'). The benchmark times the detector only (cv::resize happens outside the timed loop) and prints a face count per detector without asserting output parity, but highway/tests/hw_test_kernels.cpp checks the Highway image transform, backbone, heads and decoded tensors against the original CDataBlob flow. In the in-harness origin build the original code is compiled without OpenMP, so its single-thread numbers are fair but differ from the default top-level CMake build (USE_OPENMP ON). Origin AVX2 differs between the two README tables (33.42 ms vs 35.93 ms at 640x480), about 7 percent run-to-run spread; the Rust table uses the image crate's resize instead of OpenCV's and says it is not for result-buffer parity or accuracy. PR #383 (pszemus, merged 2026-06-28) fixed a SIGSEGV on x86 AVX2+ targets in five Highway kernels (MulAddLoop, DotProductHw, AddHw, AddInplaceHw, ReluHw) that used aligned Load/Store on 16-byte-aligned std::vector blobs; the fix switched them to LoadU/StoreU, the README numbers (MSVC on Windows, measured in May 2026) were not re-measured afterwards, and no performance effect is stated. ARM has not been tested for the Highway version. Domain note: this is CNN inference for face detection and could instead be filed under numerics-and-science / autodiff-and-ml-kernels rather than image-codecs. The older README tables (i7-7820X AVX2/AVX512, Raspberry Pi 4B) have no baseline.

notes: Every quoted README number matches (3.9x, 3.6x, 2.8x, 2.8x single-thread; 1.9x MT at 640x480; 6750.38 vs 19047.05 FPS; 7.7x vs scalar; Rust 35.93 vs 8.73 ms); metadata checked: 12.8k stars, 3.0k forks, BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2026-06-28. Kept at A despite PR #383: the fix is a crash fix (aligned to unaligned loads) that cannot have made the measured MSVC runs faster or wrong, since a misaligned aligned-load would have faulted rather than completed; if the orchestrator applies the later-fixed-bug rule strictly, the cap would be C. Shortcomings: self-baseline (original implementation) only, no external detector compared, wrong-ish category (ML inference, not image codec).
